item.text:
The archive supports two modest display ideas. Both can be prepared within Mara’s stated weekend and $30 ceiling, but neither is ready for public use: the archive records unresolved permissions and no available venue.

1. **A paper shoreline demonstration.** Recreate the low-cost workshop with movable blue paper bands against white card, showing how one repeated shape can suggest a changing shoreline. The workshop notes describe this activity, and the prototype used four sheets of card and scissors ([workshop.txt](</tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/workshop.txt>); [materials.txt](</tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/materials.txt>); [demo-notes.txt](</tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/demo-notes.txt>)). There is also a three-slit portable silhouette pattern, but the archive says the pattern cannot be publicly displayed or adapted without the collaborator’s separate written permission ([shape-diagram.txt](</tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/shape-diagram.txt>); [folded-water.txt](</tmp/work/03-rights/folded-water.txt>)). Card, scissors, and tape may no longer be available ([craft-box.txt](</tmp/work/02-assets/notes/craft-box.txt>).

   **Next steps:** Ask the collaborator for written permission before using FW-7; confirm materials are available or price replacements within the budget; arrange a venue. The old motorized lightbox was never ordered, and a projector is unavailable, so the plan should stay paper-based ([old-plan.txt](</tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/old-plan.txt>); [other-materials.txt](</tmp/work/04-resources/other-materials.txt>)).

2. **A small, text-led “Tide Lines” display.** Use the draft captions and clearly label the pier observations as informal field notes, not scientific data. The archive has captions about routes and changing water, and observations at three dates ([text-fragments.txt](</tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/text-fragments.txt>); [observations.txt](</tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/observations.txt>)). Mara’s private notebook notes and captions lack consent for public display or adaptation; the archive says to check with her first ([tide-notes.txt](</tmp/work/03-rights/tide-notes.txt>)). The historical claim about the inlet path moving inland in 1981 needs verification against the original reference before publication ([research.txt](</tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/research.txt>).

   **Next steps:** Ask Mara for permission; omit the 1981 claim unless verified; make a simple text-only layout. Up to twelve black-and-white pages may cost a flat $8 if the shared-studio printer is available, but availability is uncertain ([printing.txt](</tmp/work/02-assets/notes/printing.txt>)). The prior quote has expired, so confirm current printing cost ([printing-quote.txt](</tmp/work/04-resources/printing-quote.txt>).

I would not propose a photo- or sound-based display: the photos are absent from the archive and require separate photographer consent, while the sound recording is absent and its ownership and public-use permission are unconfirmed ([photos-index.txt](</tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/photos-index.txt>); [photo-terms.txt](</tmp/work/03-rights/photo-terms.txt>); [sound-index.txt](</tmp/work/02-assets/notes/sound-index.txt>); [sound-terms.txt](</tmp/work/03-rights/sound-terms.txt>)). The community library has no public-display table available, and no alternative venue is checked or booked ([venue.txt](</tmp/work/04-resources/venue.txt>)). Thus these are workable concepts to prepare, not confirmed public exhibits.
